title: Gaussian Orthogonal Decomposition and Quadratic Forms

items.title: Orthogonal transformations preserve the standard normal product law
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge1$, let $Z\sim N_n(0,I_n)$ have independent standard-normal coordinates, and let $U\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ satisfy $U^TU=I_n$. Then $UZ$ also has independent $N(0,1)$ coordinates. Here $I_n$ is the identity matrix and $U$ is orthogonal.
items.strategy: Compute the multivariate characteristic function after the orthogonal map, then apply finite-Borel Fourier uniqueness.

references.title: Dmitry Panchenko, MIT 18.443 Statistics for Applications, Fall 2006, Lecture 4
Yen-Chi Chen, UW STAT 512 Lecture 8: Linear Models and Multivariate Normal Distributions

items.title: Chi-square laws, including zero degrees
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For an integer $k\ge1$, let $G=(G_1,\ldots,G_k)$ have law $N_k(0,I_k)$, so its coordinates are independent $N(0,1)$ random variables. The **chi-square law with $k$ degrees of freedom**, denoted $\chi_k^2$, is the law of
$$
Q_k=\sum_{j=1}^k G_j^2=\|G\|^2.
$$
For $k=0$, define $\chi_0^2=\delta_0$, the point mass at zero. This zero-degree law records a rank-zero projection only; it is not used as a denominator in a Student or Fisher ratio. The multivariate-normal characteristic-function theorem makes the definition independent of the chosen realization of $G$.
items.strategy: Define the law of the squared Euclidean norm of a standard normal product vector, with an explicit zero-degree point mass.

references.title: Yen-Chi Chen, UW STAT 512 Lecture 8: Linear Models and Multivariate Normal Distributions
Dmitry Panchenko, MIT 18.443 Statistics for Applications, Fall 2003, Lectures 16–17

items.title: Positive-degree chi-square laws have a positive density and regular CDF
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every integer $k\ge1$, the law $\chi_k^2$ has density
$$
f_k(x)=c_k x^{k/2-1}e^{-x/2}\mathbf 1_{\{x>0\}},\qquad c_k=\frac{\sigma_{k-1}(S^{k-1})}{2(2\pi)^{k/2}}>0,
$$
where $\sigma_{k-1}$ is the polar surface measure on the unit sphere in $\mathbb R^k$. Consequently, $Q_k>0$ almost surely, and its cumulative distribution function is continuous on $\mathbb R$ and strictly increasing on $(0,\infty)$.
items.strategy: Derive the product normal density and apply polar coordinates; the resulting positive radial density gives continuity, strict increase and positive denominators.

references.title: Aditya Guntuboyina, UC Berkeley Stat 201A Fall 2019, Lecture Notes, §§5.5–5.6
Yen-Chi Chen, UW STAT 512 Lecture 8: Linear Models and Multivariate Normal Distributions
Dmitry Panchenko, MIT 18.443 Statistics for Applications, Fall 2003, Lecture 16

items.title: Orthogonal projections split a standard Gaussian into independent chi-square sums
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge1$, let $Z\sim N_n(0,I_n)$, and let $P\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be an orthogonal projection of rank $r$, where $0\le r\le n$. Then the random vectors $PZ$ and $(I_n-P)Z$ are independent, and
$$
\|PZ\|^2\sim\chi_r^2,\qquad \|(I_n-P)Z\|^2\sim\chi_{n-r}^2.
$$
The two squared norms are independent. The cases $r=0$ and $r=n$ are included, with $\chi_0^2=\delta_0$.
items.strategy: Diagonalize the finite-dimensional projection, rotate the standard normal vector and group independent coordinate blocks.

references.title: Aditya Guntuboyina, UC Berkeley Stat 201A Fall 2019, Lecture Notes, §5.6
Yen-Chi Chen, UW STAT 512 Lecture 8: Linear Models and Multivariate Normal Distributions

items.title: Student t and Fisher F laws
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a positive integer $k$, take the product probability law of an independent standard normal $G$ and an independent $Q_k\sim\chi_k^2$. The **Student t law with $k$ degrees of freedom**, denoted $t_k$, is the law of
$$T_k=\begin{cases} \displaystyle\frac{G}{\sqrt{Q_k/k}},&Q_k>0,\\ 0,&Q_k\le0. \end{cases}$$
For positive integers $r,s$, take independent $Q_r\sim\chi_r^2$ and $Q_s\sim\chi_s^2$. The **Fisher F law with degrees $(r,s)$**, denoted $F_{r,s}$, is the law of
$$F_{r,s}=\begin{cases} \displaystyle\frac{Q_r/r}{Q_s/s},&Q_s>0,\\ 0,&Q_s\le0. \end{cases}$$
The displayed piecewise maps are defined on all of $\mathbb R^2$ and are Borel measurable: each quotient is continuous on its Borel positive-denominator region, and the value on the complementary Borel nonpositive-denominator region is constant. The positive-degree chi-square lemma proves that the denominators are positive almost surely, so these versions agree almost surely with the usual quotients. Zero degrees are excluded from both definitions.
items.strategy: Define t and F as ratios under finite product probability laws with positive chi-square degrees of freedom.

references.title: Dmitry Panchenko, MIT 18.443 Statistics for Applications, Fall 2003, Lecture 16
Yen-Chi Chen, UW STAT 512 Lecture 8: Linear Models and Multivariate Normal Distributions

items.title: Student t and Fisher F CDFs are continuous and strictly increasing on their supports
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every $k\ge1$, the CDF of $t_k$ is continuous and strictly increasing on $\mathbb R$, is symmetric about zero, and has limits $0$ and $1$ at $-\infty$ and $+\infty$. For every $r,s\ge1$, the CDF of $F_{r,s}$ is continuous on $\mathbb R$, is zero on $(-\infty,0]$, and is strictly increasing on $(0,\infty)$ with limit $1$ at $+\infty$. Consequently, for each $u\in(0,1)$ each law has exactly one $u$-quantile on its support.
items.strategy: Condition on the independent chi-square variables, use dominated convergence and strict monotonicity of the inner normal or chi-square CDF.

references.title: Dmitry Panchenko, MIT 18.443 Statistics for Applications, Fall 2003, Lectures 16–17
Joshua M. Tebbs, STAT 512 Lecture Notes, Chapter 8, §8.7.1
Yen-Chi Chen, UW STAT 512 Lecture 8: Linear Models and Multivariate Normal Distributions

items.title: Normal sample mean and residual are independent, giving the exact t pivot
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Use the experiment with data space $(\mathbb R^n,\mathcal B(\mathbb R^n))$, parameter set $\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)$, and sampling law $P_{\mu,\sigma^2}=N(\mu,\sigma^2)^{\otimes n}$. Let $n\ge2$, $\sigma>0$, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be the independent coordinates of the observation. Define
$$\bar X=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nX_i,\qquad S^2=\frac1{n-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(X_i-\bar X)^2,\qquad S=\sqrt{S^2}.$$
The map $x\mapsto\bar x$ is a statistic. The sample mean $\bar X$ and residual sum $S^2$ are independent,
$$\frac{(n-1)S^2}{\sigma^2}\sim\chi_{n-1}^2,\qquad S>0\ \text{almost surely},\qquad \widetilde T:=\begin{cases} \dfrac{\bar X-\mu}{S/\sqrt n},&S>0,\\ 0,&S=0 \end{cases} \sim t_{n-1}.$$
For every $0<\alpha<1$, the interval
$$\left[\bar X-q_{n-1}(1-\alpha/2)\frac{S}{\sqrt n},\ \bar X+q_{n-1}(1-\alpha/2)\frac{S}{\sqrt n}\right]$$
has exact coverage $1-\alpha$, where $q_{n-1}(u)$ is the unique $u$-quantile of $t_{n-1}$ established in [[lem-student-t-and-f-cdfs-are-continuous-and-strictly-increasing]].
items.strategy: Standardize the iid sample, split its mean and residual projections, then invert the continuous symmetric t pivot.

references.title: Dmitry Panchenko, MIT 18.443 Statistics for Applications, Fall 2003, Lecture 17
Aditya Guntuboyina, UC Berkeley Stat 201A Fall 2019, Lecture Notes, §5.5
Joshua M. Tebbs, STAT 512 Lecture Notes, Chapter 8, §8.7.1

items.title: QR decomposition gives exact t and F pivots in the fixed Gaussian linear model
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix a deterministic matrix $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ with $n>p\ge1$ whose $p$ columns are linearly independent. Use the experiment on $(\mathbb R^n,\mathcal B(\mathbb R^n))$ indexed by $(\beta,\sigma^2)\in\mathbb R^p\times(0,\infty)$, with observation $Y=X\beta+\varepsilon$ and independent errors $\varepsilon_i\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$. Define the least-squares statistic and residual sum of squares by
$$\widehat\beta=(X^TX)^{-1}X^TY,\qquad P_X=X(X^TX)^{-1}X^T,\qquad RSS_X=\|(I_n-P_X)Y\|^2,\qquad S^2=\frac{RSS_X}{n-p},\qquad S=\sqrt{S^2}.$$
For every nonzero $c\in\mathbb R^p$,
$$\widetilde T_c:=\begin{cases} \dfrac{c^T\widehat\beta-c^T\beta}{S\sqrt{c^T(X^TX)^{-1}c}},&S>0,\\ 0,&S=0 \end{cases} \sim t_{n-p},\qquad \frac{RSS_X}{\sigma^2}\sim\chi_{n-p}^2,$$
and $\widehat\beta$ is independent of $RSS_X$, with $S>0$ almost surely.

For nested deterministic full and reduced design spaces $W_R\subset W_U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ of dimensions $p-q$ and $p$, where $q$ is an integer and $1\le q\le p<n$, let $P_R,P_U$ be the orthogonal projections onto these spaces and define $RSS_R=\|(I-P_R)Y\|^2$ and $RSS_U=\|(I-P_U)Y\|^2$. Under the null hypothesis that the mean vector belongs to $W_R$,
$$\widetilde F:=\begin{cases} \dfrac{(RSS_R-RSS_U)/q}{RSS_U/(n-p)},&RSS_U>0,\\ 0,&RSS_U=0 \end{cases} \sim F_{q,n-p}.$$
The numerator and denominator chi-square contributions are independent. All t and F denominator degrees of freedom in the statement are positive.
items.strategy: Use thin QR and an orthogonal completion to separate coefficient and residual coordinates; use nested orthogonal blocks for F.

references.title: MIT 18.S096, Regression Analysis, Lecture 6, Normal Regression Models
Yen-Chi Chen, UW STAT 512 Lecture 8: Linear Models and Multivariate Normal Distributions

items.title: An exact unknown-variance t interval for a four-point sample
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and an iid sample of size $4$ from $N(\mu,\sigma^2)$ with $\sigma>0$. For the observed values $(1,2,4,5)$, the sample mean is $\bar x=3$ and the unbiased sample variance is $s^2=10/3$. The exact $95\%$ t interval produced by the sample is
$$
\left[3-t_{3,39/40}\frac{\sqrt{10/3}}2,\ 3+t_{3,39/40}\frac{\sqrt{10/3}}2\right].
$$
The repeated-sampling coverage of this interval procedure is exactly $0.95$ under the stated normal model; this is a coverage statement about the procedure, not a probability assigned to the fixed parameter after observing these data.
items.strategy: Compute the sample mean and variance, then apply the exact t pivot and its unique central quantile.

references.title: Dmitry Panchenko, MIT 18.443 Statistics for Applications, Fall 2003, Lecture 17
Joshua M. Tebbs, STAT 512 Lecture Notes, Chapter 8, §8.7.1

items.title: A fixed-design slope contrast and nested-model F statistic
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Use the fixed design with rows $(1,-1),(1,-1),(1,1),(1,1)$ and observations $y=(1,2,4,5)^T$. The full model has intercept and slope; the reduced model has only an intercept, so the rank difference is $q=1$. The least-squares estimates are $(\widehat\beta_0,\widehat\beta_1)=(3,3/2)$, the full residual sum is $RSS_U=1$, and the reduced residual sum is $RSS_R=10$. Thus the observed slope t statistic under $H_0:\beta_1=0$ is $3\sqrt2$, and the nested-model F statistic is
$$
F=\frac{(10-1)/1}{1/(4-2)}=18.
$$
Under fixed-design normal errors with the null true, the theorem gives exact laws $t_2$ for the contrast and $F_{1,2}$ for the nested-model statistic.
items.strategy: Compute QR-equivalent least-squares coefficients and residual sums for an explicit nested fixed design.

references.title: MIT 18.S096, Regression Analysis, Lecture 6, Normal Regression Models

items.title: Rademacher errors show orthogonality alone gives neither independence nor exact t and F laws
items.statement: "An orthogonal transformation preserves independence for arbitrary independent coordinates, and orthogonality alone guarantees the exact normal-theory t and F laws."
items.strategy: Use a two-coordinate rotation to disprove independence preservation, then exhibit positive-probability zero residual denominators.
